'''Paco Axel Lagerstrom''' (February 24, 1914 &ndash; February 16, 1989) was a Swedish-American applied mathematician and aeronautical engineer. He was trained formally in mathematics, but worked for much of his career in aeronautical applications. He was known for work in applying the method of [[asymptotic expansion]] to fluid mechanics problems.<ref name="nature_2004">Narasimha, R. (2004) [http://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v432/n7019/full/432807a.html ''Divide, conquer and unify''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080520041320/http://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v432/n7019/full/432807a.html |date=2008-05-20 }}, [[Nature (journal)|Nature]] '''432'''(7019), 807.</ref> Several of his works have become classics, including "Matched Asymptotic Expansions: Ideas And Techniques".<ref name="springer_1988">Lagerstrom, P. A. (1988) Matched Asymptotic Expansions: Ideas And Techniques, Springer.</ref>

==Biography==
He was born on February 24, 1914, in [[Oskarshamn]], [[Sweden]].

Lagerstrom earned bachelor's and master's degrees, in 1935 and 1939 respectively, at the [[Stockholm University]].<ref name="pu_1991"/> He then came to America as a graduate student at [[Princeton University]], earning a PhD in 1942 in mathematics under [[Salomon Bochner]]<ref name="Bochner"/> with a dissertation entitled "Measure and Integral in Partially Ordered Spaces". During this time, Lagerstrom was also a mathematics instructor.

He left Princeton in 1944 to work briefly at [[Bell Aircraft]] in Niagara Falls, New York until 1945,<ref name="pu_1991"/> after which he worked for a similarly brief period at [[Douglas Aircraft Company|Douglas Aircraft]] in Santa Monica.<ref name="galcit">[http://www.galcit.caltech.edu/history/index.html ''GALCIT: The First 75 Years''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070415120112/http://www.galcit.caltech.edu/history/index.html |date=2007-04-15 }}.</ref> While he had already published significant results in pure mathematics,<ref name="bams_251">McMillan, B. and Lagerstrom, P. (1945) [https://www.ams.org/bull/1945-51-04/S0002-9904-1945-08323-2/home.html ''Extension of a theorem of Bochner on expressing functionals as Riemann integrals''], [[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] '''51''', 251-258.</ref><ref name="bams_535">Lagerstrom, P. (1945) [http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?verb=Display&version=1.0&service=UI&handle=euclid.bams/1183507189&page=record ''A proof of a theorem on commutative matrices''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607184644/http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?verb=Display&version=1.0&service=UI&handle=euclid.bams/1183507189&page=record |date=2011-06-07 }}, [[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] '''51''', 535-536.</ref> he was, by this time, firmly interested in its applications to fluid dynamic and aerodynamic problems. In 1946, Lagerstrom was recruited by [[Hans W. Liepmann|Hans Liepmann]] to the [[Guggenheim Aeronautical Laboratory]] at [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]].<ref name="galcit"/> He was later promoted to Professor of Aeronautics in 1952 and Professor of Applied Mathematics in 1967,<ref name="galcit"/> having departed only briefly to the [[University of Paris]] in 1960–1961 as visiting professor on a [[List of Guggenheim Fellowships awarded in 1960|Guggenheim Fellowship]].<ref name="pu_1991"/>

He died on February 16, 1989.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://calteches.library.caltech.edu/609/2/Obituaries.pdf | title=Obituaries - Frederick C. Lindvall 1903-1989 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210429164539/http://calteches.library.caltech.edu/609/2/Obituaries.pdf | archive-date=2021-04-29 }}</ref>

==Publications==
His book "Laminar flow theory", initially published in 1964 in the Theory of Laminar flows, edited by F.K.Moore, is still considered as the standard textbook for fluid mechanics.
